newsitem.title: USA: American Intl begins asphalt expansion.
newsitem.headline: American Intl begins asphalt expansion.

text.p: American International Petroleum Corp said Thursday it has received all the necessary permits for the expansion of its 20,000 barrel-per-day vacuum distillation unit at its Lake Charles, La., refinery as an asphalt facility and has begun the construction of storage tanks and an asphalt polymerization unit.

The company noted it had announced a $6 million 12.5 percent interim loan commitment to fund the expansion with funding to become available in three $2 million stages. Although the first traunch did not close as announced on June 28, the company has been able to draw down funds.
It did so in multiple closings to start phase one construction which primarily entails asphalt tanks and a polymerization unit.

Based on a study performed by Purvin & Gertz Inc, American International said, it plans to initially operate the VDU at 7,000 to 10,000 barrels per day to produce primarily conventional paving asphalt, vacuum gas oil, and diesel.

At these levels, the study estimates the annual revenues from the sale of the various products to range between $40 and $50 million, with attractive operating margins. As asphalt product manufacturing levels increase, revenues and operation margins should be substantially higher, the company said.

On June 25, American International said, it signed an exclusive agreement with Coastal Corp's Coastal Refining and Marketing Inc unit to use the Lake Charles facility to provide terminaling, blending and polymerizing of Coastal's asphalt during the asphalt off-season beginning in November 1996 and continuing until mid-April 1997.
After mid-April, the agreement calls for Coastal to purchase and market all conventional and polymerized paving asphalt produced by American International.
